message.content:
Now I understand the full picture. The `digits(y)` function returns the number of significant digits. If `y->sz == 1` and `y->p[0] != 0`, then `digits(y) == 1`. The check `digits(y) > 2 || y->p[1] > 1` will evaluate `y->p[1]` even when `digits(y) == 1` (because of short-circuit evaluation: `digits(y) > 2` is false, so it evaluates `y->p[1] > 1`).

So the vulnerability triggers when:
1. A bigint has `sz == 1` (only one limb allocated)
2. `mpz_get_int` is called on it

Now, how do we create a bigint with `sz == 1`? Looking at `mpz_set_int`, when `(u & LC) == 0`, `len = 1`. This happens when the value fits in one limb.

But `mrb_bint_new_int` is called from `mrb_bint_mul_ii` etc. when integer operations overflow. The result of those operations would be large (needing 2 limbs).
